decisions.statement: The input is reached only where the call names no file for a body.
A terminal is nothing piped in.
An input with no byte is nothing piped in.
A read of the input waits a stated while and never without end.
The while begins again at every byte that arrives.
An input that had nothing before the while ran out is nothing piped in.
An input that went quiet part way through a body is refused rather than taken as that body.
An input that went quiet part way is told from an input that would not open.
A body piped in where every path names a file is left unread.
A body that is not text is carried through as the bytes the body is.
A body holding a line that begins with `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` is marked.
This module reaches the disk only at the input itself.
The wording a caller is told to say instead is handed in by that caller.
An input no second descriptor can be opened on is answered as an input that would not open.

definition: what a command is handed on standard input
